title: Universal arrows give coherent infinity-categorical adjoints
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $R:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a functor of quasicategories. Suppose that, for every object $y\in\mathcal Y$, there are an object $x_y\in\mathcal X$ and an edge $u_y:y\to R(x_y)$ such that, for every $z\in\mathcal X$, the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(x_y,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(y,Rz),\qquad v\longmapsto R(v)\circ u_y$$
is an equivalence of spaces. Then $R$ has a coherent left adjoint $L:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$. In particular there are coherent natural transformations $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Y}\to RL$ and $\epsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal X}$, the maps $v\mapsto R(v)\circ\eta_y$ are equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(Ly,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(y,Rz)$ natural in both variables, and $R\epsilon\circ\eta R\simeq1_R$, $\epsilon L\circ L\eta\simeq1_L$. The hypotheses are objectwise: the initially given $x_y,u_y$ need not vary functorially. The supplied data determine universal arrows; they are not themselves postulated to be a functor.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 6.2.6.1 (02FV), local existence criterion; Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1) identifies the induced mapping-space equivalences. The unit/counit and triangle identities are the adjunction structure in that criterion. Both pages read online, not archived in literature/. Mapping spaces use the right-pinched convention, checked against Kerodon Propositions 4.6.5.5 and 4.6.5.10. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-join-cartesian-realization] to $R$. Write $E=E_R$ and $p:E\to\Delta^1$, with full fibers $E_0=\mathcal Y$, $E_1=\mathcal X$ and the explicit coherent cartesian transport witness $h$ for $R$. An edge $u_y:y\to R(x_y)$ defines a mixed edge $f_y:y\to x_y$ of $E$, using the mixed-edge correspondence of that node. Its mapping-space isomorphisms identify precomposition with $f_y$ on maps into $z\in E_1$ with $v\mapsto R(v)\circ u_y$. No naturality of the initial choices $x_y,u_y$ is used.

Test $f_y$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The required inner-fibration hypothesis holds because $p$ is cartesian. If $z\in E_1$, the two bottom mapping spaces in the criterion are $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(1,1)=\Delta^0$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(0,1)=\Delta^0$. Its top map is the equivalence in the hypothesis, by step 1; therefore the square is a homotopy pullback. If $z\in E_0$, its upper left and lower left corners are both empty: $\operatorname{Map}_E(x_y,z)=\varnothing$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(1,0)=\varnothing$. Its lower right corner is $\Delta^0$; the homotopy pullback of any space over $\Delta^0$ with $\varnothing$ is empty. Thus this square too is a homotopy pullback. All vertices of $E$ lie in one of these two fibers, so $f_y$ is $p$-cocartesian.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.3 (01TQ), cocartesian dual over the interval; using the existing general mapping-square criterion.

proof.text: The only nonidentity edge of $\Delta^1$ is $0\to1$. For each object over $0$, step 2 supplies its cocartesian lift. For an identity edge at either base vertex, take the identity edge of the chosen object of $E$: the unital clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] identifies precomposition by this edge with the identity homotopy class. Choose identity representatives for the two horizontal maps in its mapping square in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]; the square is then a homotopy pullback. Thus identity edges are cocartesian as well. Since $p$ is already inner, the definition [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] now says that $p$ is cocartesian. It is therefore both cartesian and cocartesian. This argument covers an empty fiber without choosing an object in it.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1 (02FV), sufficiency, promotion from the mixed cocartesian lifts to a cocartesian fibration.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-bicartesian-interval-adjunction] to this $p$ and the coherent cartesian witness $h$ from step 1. Its hypotheses now hold by steps 1 and 3, so it supplies $L:E_0\to E_1$, a coherent adjunction to the specified functor $R:E_1\to E_0$, and its natural unit and counit. Substituting the strict fiber identifications $E_0=\mathcal Y$ and $E_1=\mathcal X$ in its conclusion gives exactly the displayed mapping equivalences $v\mapsto R(v)\circ\eta_y$ and both coherent triangle homotopies of this item. The resulting functor is obtained by coherent transport; there is no assertion that the initially chosen pairs form a functor.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.5.4 (02FN), bicartesian direction; Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1), adjunct maps.

proof_origin.place: Sufficiency proof of Proposition 6.2.6.1: explicit relative join, mapping-space cocartesian test, then bicartesian interval transport (024K, 024F, 01TQ, 02FN). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived. Replaces the erroneous comma-right-fibration argument.

Checked the sources on Kerodon: 02FV sufficiency builds the relative join C*_C D, which is cartesian over Delta^1 (5.2.3.15/024K, with h witnessing G as contravariant transport); it shows each universal arrow gives a cocartesian edge (5.1.2.3), so U is cocartesian; 02FN (6.2.5.4) then gives the left adjoint, and the right adjoint is the contravariant transport. The four steps follow this exactly. Item statement is unchanged, objectwise, with the right map orientation and unit/counit types; nothing is weakened. Step 1: in Y*_Y X, mixed edges y->x are exactly pairs with sigma: y->Rx. Mapping spaces: Map(y,x) is isomorphic to Map_Y(y,Rx) and Map(x,y) is empty. In a 2-simplex sigma restricts to u and R(v), so precomposition corresponds to v->R(v)u. Step 2: inner because cartesian. For z in E1 the square is pt/pt under the hypothesis equivalence; for z in E0 both left corners are empty, so it is a homotopy pullback. Step 3 (elementary): identity edges are cocartesian by the unital clause, and the lift over 0->1 comes from step 2; the empty-fiber case is covered. Step 4: hypotheses of the bicartesian node hold, h is over Delta^1, and the variance L:E0->E1 left adjoint to R is correct. New nodes are statement-only and self-contained, with TeX correct and three kinds of search recorded. Tested R=id, X empty, X=Y=pt, and one or both fibers empty. Neither new node restates the item. Duplicate grep (02FN/024K/02FV/02FM, bicartesian, transport, relative join): the pointwise-adjoint and parametric-universal-arrows nodes are users of this item, not duplicates; the fiberwise-relative-join and arrow-join nodes are about other matters; the 02FM hits in sec-smooth-base-change are unrelated Stacks tags. lean.statement: theorem infinity_local_adjoint_criterion (X Y : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory X] [Quasicategory Y] (R : X ⟶ Y) (h : ∀ y : Y _⦋0⦌, ∃ x : X _⦋0⦌, ∃ u : (mappingSpace Y y (R.app _ x)) _⦋0⦌, ∀ z : X _⦋0⦌, IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (localAdjointComparison R y x u z)) : ∃ (L : Y ⟶ X) (η : SSet.Edge (diagramVertex (𝟙 Y)) (diagramVertex (L ≫ R))) (ε : SSet.Edge (diagramVertex (R ≫ L)) (diagramVertex (𝟙 X))), (∃ t : ((ihom Y).obj X) _⦋2⦌, ((ihom Y).obj X).δ 2 t = ((ihom Y).map L).app _ η.edge ∧ ((ihom Y).obj X).δ 0 t = ((MonoidalClosed.pre L).app X).app _ ε.edge ∧ ((ihom Y).obj X).δ 1 t = ((ihom Y).obj X).σ 0 (diagramVertex L)) ∧ (∃ t : ((ihom X).obj Y) _⦋2⦌, ((ihom X).obj Y).δ 2 t = ((MonoidalClosed.pre R).app Y).app _ η.edge ∧ ((ihom X).obj Y).δ 0 t = ((ihom X).map R).app _ ε.edge ∧ ((ihom X).obj Y).δ 1 t = ((ihom X).obj Y).σ 0 (diagramVertex R)) ∧ ∀ y : Y _⦋0⦌, ∃ u : (mappingSpace Y y (R.app _ (L.app _ y))) _⦋0⦌, u.1 = (evaluation Y Y y).app _ η.edge ∧ ∀ z : X _⦋0⦌, IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (localAdjointComparison R y (L.app _ y) u z)
lean.note: Uses the landed mapping-composition theorem for its canonical composition class. Unit and counit are actual functor-space edges, and both triangles are full functor-space 2-simplices. Their same unit fixes the displayed mapping comparisons. No arbitrary comparison map or unspecified naturality/triangle proposition occurs.
